name: An Intergigantes Association
description: Intergigantes has brought Avian out of isolation. Iovinus can now offer more than an observer's chair: a negotiated place in a united Verenia. Begin with the courts, colleges and municipal charters. A separate accession act will decide who governs the common country, and Katrina must be able to read it before she signs.

name: A Charter We Can Sign
description: Offer Erie an equal council with defined responsibilities, common courts and room for practical cooperation. Vincent may accept this constitution, ask to preside within strictly limited powers, or refuse. His chairmanship would require our explicit consent and convey no sovereignty over Eyrie. Iovinus must decide which shared powers he can honour after the congress has dispersed.

name: Officers at One Table
description: The shared staff will have to turn familiar suspicions into questions that can be answered on a map. Supply officers will compare their plans while signallers practise carrying a report across the old divide. Iovinus expects each officer to know what he can promise, and when he must ask the government whose troops he serves.

name: Specifications Worth Sharing
description: The same replacement part should not require a different drawing on each side of the frontier. Put the charter's technical services to work comparing specifications and production methods. Shared services will help the participating workshops, while Eyrie's engineers gain an opportunity to develop their industrial knowledge. Useful cooperation can begin with a part that fits.

name: An Order to Give Back
description: The civilian workshops requisitioned for the frontier army have received their release orders. The command has refused to hand them over. Its officers invoke readiness, but the authority that allowed the requisitions also set their limits. Iovinus must enforce those limits against his own military establishment or protect it at the expense of the charter's credibility.

name: Defence by Agreement
description: The staff can draw a common plan, but it cannot promise another government's soldiers. Iovinus will put a defensive league before Erie, with duties clear enough to survive the first alarm at the frontier. Existing alliances must be respected, and Katrina will have to answer for Avian in her own name. The officers may prepare the maps while the governments consider the signatures.

name: The Workshops Return to Work
description: Returning a key is only the beginning. Civilian production needs usable premises, replacement equipment and workers who can plan beyond the next requisition notice. The works office will inspect what the army has returned and hear the owners' estimates. A workshop promised back must become a place where someone can earn a living again.

name: A Border Without Emergency Orders
description: The army will still guard the country. Its task can become clearer now that every consignment, workshop and journey need not remain at its disposal. A dependable settlement gives Iovinus partners whose consent matters and soldiers whose authority has an agreed boundary. The frontier should be secure enough to let ordinary business proceed without asking headquarters for permission.

name: Eyrie's Own Work
description: The shared settlement has failed. The refusal may have come before a ceasefire, before a treaty, or at the final congress; the government across the line may no longer be able to keep its word. None of that repairs a road in Eyrie. We will honour whatever agreements remain valid, without claiming ones that never existed, and turn the work of recovery towards our own country. Iovinus promised to seek security without conquest. A disappointing answer does not release him from that choice.

name: The Last Campaign
description: Iovinus's officers promise a campaign that will finally make perpetual vigilance unnecessary. He understands the attraction, and how readily headquarters finds reasons to remain indispensable. Choosing their campaign closes the negotiated road with Erie. The duke must decide what Eyrie will take by force and what his own command will have to surrender afterwards, so that victory becomes more than the next mobilisation.

name: Break the Rival Line
description: Eyrie's claim has not persuaded Erie to yield. Iovinus will prepare a demand backed by the prospect of war, accepting responsibility for a contest that ancestry alone cannot resolve. An existing peace must still be respected. The preparations provide grounds to fight the rival House; the decision to send the army remains a separate and deliberate act.

name: Orders That Reach the Column
description: A good order arriving late may be less useful than a poor one already understood. Train liaison officers to carry the same picture of the field between headquarters, engineers and the marching columns. Practical work with signals will help Iovinus discover where his command's confidence outruns its knowledge, and give the troops a better chance of receiving instructions they can use.

name: Keep the Columns Supplied
description: Quartermasters cannot feed a column with the assurance that another district ought to have sent its carts. Improve loading plans, transport maintenance and the means of reporting a shortage. The army's demands travel through villages and workshops before reaching a depot. Understanding that journey will matter when those same places ask what the end of the campaign has changed.

name: Victory and the Garrison
description: The rival army has been defeated and the territorial peace established. Eyrie's officers can still name a reason to maintain emergency command in every district. Iovinus must decide whether to return ordinary administration and economic life to civilian hands or make military tutelage the basis of the settlement. Neither decision will settle the livelihoods waiting outside the headquarters gate.

name: Montague's Unsent Reply
description: Montague has an unfinished reply to an older letter from Rosaline, and a question for Iovinus: must private words still receive military approval? The answer will reach beyond this correspondence. Civilian post can carry knowledge and ordinary business at a continuing administrative cost. Command supervision will keep communications useful to headquarters while reminding every writer that an officer may be reading.

name: Dates for Coming Home
description: The end of emergency administration must have dates that a workshop or household can plan around. Publish a schedule for returning civilian premises and responsibilities, and prepare the building work that will make their use possible. Iovinus will have to accept demands arriving without the discipline of a military return, and answer people who are no longer awaiting his next command.

name: The District Commands
description: The garrison will remain an institution of government. Give district commanders permanent responsibilities for coordination, supply and readiness, with staff trained to make those responsibilities workable. Their competence may bring a dependable rhythm to the settlement. It will also carry military authority into decisions that inhabitants might otherwise have made without asking permission.

name: The Work Waiting After War
description: Enough time has passed for the chosen order to encounter ordinary needs. Under civilian administration, returning reservists need instruction and premises before service can become a trade. Under military government, civilian repairs compete with the command's orders for machine time. Hear the workshop reports and decide who will bear the cost of the transition.

name: Useful Trades
description: A former soldier can bring patience, skill and confidence to a workshop without knowing how to operate its machinery. Expand civilian production and the industrial knowledge that sustains it. The programme must build on the answer already given to the returning reservists; a new building alone cannot make an unfunded promise of training disappear.

name: A Permanent District Staff
description: The military districts need more than a succession of temporary detachments. Establish permanent staff and workshops capable of maintaining the equipment their orders require. The arrangement will make command more dependable while binding industrial work closely to its needs. Civilian contracts, where authorised, will still have to find their place within that hierarchy.

name: Registers for the Districts
description: A garrison report cannot replace a civil register. Iovinus orders the district staff to reconcile property records, tax rolls and transport maps so that the two duchies can be administered as a country rather than as an army's temporary possessions.

name: Inspect the Working Day
description: A prepared parade tells Iovinus what a district can arrange for his arrival. An ordinary working day will tell him more about the order he has created. Examine deliveries and workshop schedules, then visit after the officials have had time to put his instructions into practice. The important question is what happens when nobody expects the duke to be watching.

name: The Road That Stays Open
description: The road that carried the campaign now carries other journeys. Improve its future through the construction knowledge gathered in the settlement, and look at the habits taking root along it. Iovinus wanted a final victory. Its meaning will be found in whether travellers can leave an emergency behind, or merely pass from one permission to the next.

name: No Unfinished Frontier
description: Avian has chosen true neutrality rather than Intergigantes. Iovinus's officers regard its frontier as the last gap in Verenia; his civilian advisers hear the dangerous promise of one more campaign before peace. The duke will demand incorporation openly. That demand does not erase the settlement with Erie or the obligations of an existing pact.

name: Orders Beyond the Surrender
description: The garrison can secure a bridge; it cannot settle every dispute carried across it. Avian's clerks ask who will hear appeals, pay the workshops and release the requisitioned wagons. Iovinus must decide whether local institutions will bind his officers or a permanent commission will answer for them. A subject government asked to surrender its remaining powers will receive guarantees, not a second ultimatum disguised as consent.

name: A Province, Not a Garrison
description: The last temporary supply office is ready to become a permanent workshop. Iovinus receives its estimate alongside the register of Avian petitions. The soldiers have done what a campaign can do; incorporation now rests on pay, law and repair. End the provisional administration without pretending that the settlement's obligations end with it.

name: A Court with an Ending
description: Herzland's offices now answer to Verenia. Among the papers reaching our chancery are requests concerning the imperial household. Before anyone offers to govern in Grover's name, we must establish where he is and whether we can lawfully answer for his care. An undertaking to protect a sovereign must also say when our authority ends.

name: The Household File
description: A portrait, a rumour and an old court allowance cannot tell us who lives behind a palace door. The household clerks will compare testimony with the surviving records and establish what has become of Grover. They owe the council an honest answer, even if that answer leaves the proposed regent without a ward.

name: The Verenian Regency
description: The mandate must distinguish care for Grover from ownership of his future. Verenia will administer Herzland under a temporary title, while the succession articles prepare a crown with authority of its own. If Grover is already of age, the work concerns the transition to his government; it cannot make him a child again.

name: Who May Be Heard
description: A court teaches through its doors as much as through its books. Some visitors arrive with polished speeches; others bring accounts that contradict the official history. We must decide whether Grover hears those disagreements himself or receives the account his advisers consider fit to place before him.

name: The Inconvenient Petition
description: A petitioner has named someone whose support our government values. The evidence has passed through the same office that recorded our guarantees, and Grover has asked to hear the case. A judgement will teach him what our promises mean when keeping them becomes personally expensive.

name: The Capital's Registers
description: Griffenheim's clerks possess shelves of overlapping grants and obligations. Reconcile the capital's records with those of its surrounding districts, so that a household can discover which office must answer its claim. The regency needs an administration that will still make sense when another sovereign signs its orders.

name: Herzland's District Books
description: The capital's settlement must travel beyond its gates. District officers will compare their rolls, settle conflicting jurisdictions and recognise the inhabitants whom the new administration is meant to serve. Their books should describe a country ready to govern itself, not a collection of offices dependent on our court.

name: Work for Verenia
description: Herzland cannot become the sole occupation of the Verenian government. Our own workshops need premises, equipment and orders that will survive the end of the regency. Investment at home gives the returning administration something more useful to offer than memories of the imperial court.

name: The Meaning of Service
description: Grover has asked to examine the work behind a military report. Quartermasters would begin with depots, hospitals and the journey of a consignment. The territorial officers would begin with command, responsibility and the duty to answer for an order. Either education must include the moment when our own authority ceases.

name: The Articles of Succession
description: A promise to relinquish power deserves more than a place in a ceremonial speech. The articles will name the country Grover is to govern, the resources its government will receive and the limits of Verenia's continuing obligations. Our signatories must be prepared to honour them when the imperial seal passes to another hand.

name: A Crown Made Ready
description: The crown is the simplest object to prepare. The harder work lies in the ministries, army offices and accounts that must answer to its wearer. Let those arrangements be completed now, so that adulthood and a secure peace can bring the promised transfer without another excuse from the regent's desk.

name: The Civil Settlement
description: The people of Herzland require courts, workshops and a government that answers in its own name. The council may undertake that work without accepting an imperial regency. Grover's protection, if he is here, need not make his future the business of our state. Let the civil administration rest on the authority we are willing to exercise ourselves.

name: The Emperor's Public Oath
description: Grover returns to a country whose future cannot be settled by his surname alone. Before the assembled deputies and household witnesses, he will bind the crown to the settlement that brought him home.

name: Open the Reconstruction Offices
description: The first petitions concern roofs, wages and workshops whose doors have remained shut since the fighting. Local engineers and elected councils must turn those petitions into work that families can see from their own streets.

name: A Charter for the Crown
description: The imperial signature must have a place in the law, and the law must remain legible without it. Ministers, deputies and the sovereign will set out who answers for each decision and how a citizen may challenge it.

name: Across the Vereni Border
description: Verenia was Grover's home before it became his neighbour. Resident envoys and visiting scholars can preserve that familiarity between two independent governments, each responsible to its own people.

name: The Workshops Reopen
description: A repaired factory needs more than a new sign above the gate. Apprentices, foregriffs and engineers will compare the methods that survived the war and train a generation able to improve upon them.

name: Petitions Before Privilege
description: An ordinary household should not need an introduction at court to obtain a hearing. Provincial judges and public clerks will establish a route from the smallest petition to a reasoned answer, even when a powerful name stands on the other side.

name: The Service Oath
description: Grover remembers the officers who taught him that command begins with responsibility. The army's new service articles will place the defence of the country under lawful civilian authority and give its soldiers a clear duty to the communities behind them.

name: A University of the Settlement
description: The rebuilt lecture halls will welcome students whose families once stood on opposite sides of the war. Public laboratories and open appointments can make the university a shared undertaking that outlasts the ceremonies of restoration.

name: Provision the Home Army
description: Quartermasters have brought the ministry a practical list: reliable tools, sound equipment and workshops close enough to maintain them. The home army will be provisioned for the defence of the settlement and the people living within it.

name: The Work of a Reign
description: The crown has returned to daily life. Its worth will be measured in hearings kept, classrooms opened and promises honoured when they become inconvenient. Grover must now learn to govern within the institutions he helped to establish.

name: The Language of the Schoolroom
description: A school inspector brings Vincent three exercise books: Aquileian prose, Griffish arithmetic, and a local song written as its singer speaks. All belong to Erie. Avian's language quarrel warns us what happens when the court mistakes its own speech for everyone's education. Our teachers must first count the children whom their lessons cannot reach.

name: An Aquileian Curriculum
description: Erie's Aquileian inheritance can offer more than courtly manners. Affordable primers and a common written standard will connect village lessons to a substantial literature of science and history. Vincent will fund teacher training in Aquileian while keeping local speech welcome in the classroom. Cultural kinship gives our schools a direction; their administration remains Erie's responsibility.

name: Two Living Languages
description: An Aquileian-speaking child should not have to forget home to learn Griffish, nor should a Griffish-speaking child be excluded from Erie's public life. Parallel readers and teachers trained in both languages will make the first lesson comprehensible and the second language attainable. The extra expense buys a curriculum that more families can trust.

name: Journals Beyond the Court
description: Aquileian scientific journals too often end their journey on a noble's shelf. A public translation bureau will purchase subscriptions, explain unfamiliar terms, and circulate practical extracts among technical schools. Wireless theory and electrical measurement will become subjects our own students can investigate, rather than marvels reported from distant academies.

name: District Teacher Colleges
description: Printing two versions of a textbook cannot replace a teacher who understands both. District colleges will train instructors to explain arithmetic, mechanics, and electrical experiments across the language divide. Scholarships for village candidates will carry these methods home, while shared examinations let an apprentice continue studying beyond the district of their birth.

name: A Place for Local Histories
description: The school standard need not become the measure of every story. Town libraries will collect songs, family records, and testimony in the dialects in which they survive, with translations beside them. When a village finds its own history on a public shelf, the cultural settlement becomes something its inhabitants have helped to write.

name: Scholarships in Public Trust
description: A capable pupil should not need a relative at Vincent's court to reach a laboratory. A permanent endowment will award scholarships through published examinations and require its scholars to teach or serve in public institutions. Erie's cultural choice will thus leave a durable inheritance: trained teachers, accessible learning, and researchers accountable to their own country.

name: The Language of Public Service
description: Iovinus receives a petition from a parish teacher whose pupils can recite an imperial lesson but cannot explain it in their own words. Eyrie's offices face the same problem with recruits and clerks. Avian's argument over language belongs here too: the House must decide how its Herzland inheritance can become an education its people actually share.

name: The Herzland School Tradition
description: The imperial written tradition gives Eyrie access to generations of scholarship. A Griffish curriculum, supported by modern primers and trained teachers, will connect parish schools to that wider body of knowledge. Iovinus can honour the Herzland's intellectual inheritance through an independent school system, with lessons explained patiently wherever a local dialect remains the language of home.

name: Two Living Languages
description: Eyrie's Griffish institutions can make room for Aquileian-speaking neighbours without abandoning their own inheritance. Bilingual readers and equal access to public examinations will let families approach the schoolhouse with confidence. Teachers will begin with the language a pupil knows and teach the other as an additional skill, preserving a shared civic life across the borderland's different voices.

name: A Common Technical Lexicon
description: A workshop manual is of little use when every instructor gives a different name to the same part. Engineers and schoolmasters will prepare Griffish reference works from the Herzland's technical literature, with familiar local terms indexed alongside them. Consistent descriptions and tested examples will help Eyrie's workshops turn formal instruction into better industrial practice.

name: The College of Interpreters
description: Our bilingual settlement needs people who can carry a precise meaning between languages. The new college will train teachers, technical translators, and public interpreters through practical work with machines and instruments. Its graduates will make industrial manuals and electrical research usable on either side of a linguistic boundary, beginning with Eyrie's own schools.

name: Open the Parish Archives
description: Registers and chronicles tell a richer story than the chancery's official histories alone. Parish archives will receive funds for conservation, public catalogues, and translations of records that younger readers can no longer understand. Keeping these voices accessible will let Eyrie's inhabitants recognise their communities within the House's cultural settlement.

name: Fellowships for Civic Service
description: Iovinus will establish fellowships for talented pupils from every district, awarded through public examinations. Their recipients will return as teachers, researchers, and trained civil servants. Whether their early lessons followed the Herzland standard or a bilingual reader, they will share the duty to make knowledge useful to the country that supported their studies.

name: The Griffenheim Settlement
description: The imperial attack on a signatory has ended in defeat, and the peace conference has left Griffenheim in our hands. Victory has brought responsibilities which the Verenia charter never expected. We may offer a limited civilian reconstruction mandate, with a public account of its work and a fixed end. The charter does not oblige us to accept an imperial crown.

name: The Household's Record
description: The fate of Grover VI cannot be settled by an inventory of the palace. Before writing a single dynastic clause, the commission must distinguish a living child from an adult, a confirmed death from an unverified report, and a household here from one sheltered elsewhere. Its report will confer no title or guardianship.

name: Contracts for a Living City
description: Griffenheim needs workshops, roofs and functioning public services. The reconstruction commission can establish a civilian workshop in the city, or invest its effort in construction methods which municipal crews can use themselves. Contracts will be paid for as public works, never as rewards for a new imperial court.

name: Open the Technical Archives
description: Behind the imperial seals are useful surveys, machine drawings and inspection records. Let civilian engineers catalogue them and publish the work that can restore production. Access to these papers carries no authority over the dynasty whose seals once protected them.

name: A Voluntary Technical Protocol
description: Surviving independent charter governments may share technical publications and workshop standards with us. Where a House has lawfully joined the unified country, its engineers instead ask the civilian council to authorize a domestic programme. Each proposal needs an explicit answer. Reconstruction can continue even if it is declined.

name: Publish the Mandate's Accounts
description: The commission must account for the factories it commissioned, the papers it released and the staff it still keeps from ordinary service. A temporary administration cannot renew itself by declaring its own work indispensable. The municipal representatives will read its estimates before deciding whether another funded year justifies delaying the handover.

name: One Final Funded Year
description: The unfinished repairs have names and addresses in the commission's final estimate. One more year's appropriation will keep its crews and research office at work, with municipal officials learning the accounts they must inherit. The closing date will remain on the first page. A temporary mandate must end even when its engineers can still find something worth repairing.

name: Return the Commission's Keys
description: The municipal offices are ready to receive the contracts, survey books and keys. The commission's engineers will leave their drawings with the people who must answer for the next repair. Ordinary administration will have fewer extraordinary powers and no special mandate to invoke when a workshop asks why its bill remains unpaid.

name: What the Victory Leaves Us
description: The Empire attacked a member of our charter; Avian answered, and the peace has left Griffenheim in our keeping. Katrina knows how easily a victorious guardian becomes another master. Before the officers put away their maps, she will ask Iovinus and Vincent what a settlement in the Herzland must promise the Houses that survived the war.

name: A Name Is Not a Household
description: Grover VI appears in petitions, inventories and proposed proclamations. None can tell Katrina whether a living child is actually in her care. Establish his circumstances before discussing guardianship. An adult needs no regent, a foreign household has its own responsibilities, and uncertainty must not be dressed as a death notice or an arrival.

name: Orders for the City
description: A workshop in Griffenheim asks whether its next order will be paid in coin or another promise of national salvation. Katrina sends for the civilian estimates. Reopening productive work will give the city something more dependable than the arrival of a new banner; where premises cannot be opened, its engineers can still improve the methods of reconstruction.

name: The Herzland Agreement
description: The Houses' original peace must survive the settlement beyond Verenia. With Grover present as a living minor, Katrina can propose a regency ending at his majority; a civil compact offers another course. Each independent government must answer freely. A lawfully absorbed House instead debates the text through its own estates within the unified country. Incorporation supplies no automatic assent.

name: A Place Among the Learners
description: The technical schools need tools, teachers and permission to question a confident answer. Bring workshop experience into their classrooms and share their discoveries with industry. If Grover is a child in our care, he should encounter that work himself. Public education has its own purpose whether or not a future monarch sits at a desk.

name: The Price of Readiness
description: Katrina's reservist system taught Avian the value of knowing who would answer a summons. Beyond Verenia, the council must decide how that service can be sustained. A common supply office would negotiate competing demands across the whole settlement. Territorial reserves would rely on officers and stores close to home. Iovinus wants to know who may call them out; Vincent wants to know who will pay when they do.

name: Let the Complaint Be Heard
description: A petition against the reconstruction office has reached the council. The petitioner is neither a courtier nor a convenient witness to our generosity. Give the complaint an ordinary hearing, even where it embarrasses Katrina's administration. A child learning government, if present, should see that a respectful bow does not oblige its author to withdraw an objection.

name: Streets Worth Coming Home To
description: Behind the repaired public facades, families still share damaged rooms and workshops wait for reliable access. Send construction specialists through the residential quarters with the engineers who learned their trade during the war. Their experience should now help make a staircase sound, a street passable and a delivery ordinary.

name: What the Houses Keep
description: The constitutional guarantees must protect Verenia's institutions when respecting them becomes inconvenient. Independent Houses keep their governments; constituent estates keep their charter rights within the unified country. The courts, agreed obligations and limits bind Katrina's administration in either case.

name: The Date on the Last Page
description: A regency has an ending even when its guardians still have unfinished business. Grover's majority ends their authority over a minor. Under the agreed settlement he may become constitutional head of the Avian-Herzland state, bound by Verenia's reserved institutions. Neither unfinished lessons nor an inconvenient birthday can justify prolonging childhood by decree.

name: A Union Without a Throne
description: The civil compact rests on the Houses' consent and the obligations they can answer for. If Grover's death is confirmed, it must acknowledge the loss without inventing a successor. Where he is adult, abroad or unaccounted for, it must respect those different circumstances. The work of governing can continue without claiming to speak through him.

name: An Ordinary Border
description: The frontier should become a place where a carrier checks a destination, not where another proclamation begins. Complete the limited settlement of the Herzland and keep Verenia's Houses within their agreed constitutional relationship. A constitutional future or a civilian one must give those living here reasons to trust tomorrow's ordinary business.

name: The Verenian Convention
description: The River countries have shown how common work can become common government. Our Houses must write their own settlement. The House calling the convention will seek the constitutional presidency, but its delegates must explain how that office will answer to the country. Towns bring their customs and courts to the table; surviving governments bring powers they will not surrender on a promise alone.

name: One Customs Schedule
description: Merchants can cross a peaceful frontier and still pay for the same cargo twice. A common tariff must survive its first encounter with a laden wagon and two clerks trained to keep different accounts. The Houses will reconcile their schedules and receipts until a carrier can cross with papers that mean the same thing at either post.

name: Roads and Common Workshops
description: A bridge cannot stop where the survey changes its letterhead. Engineers from the participating districts will agree on loads, deliveries and maintenance. New civilian workshops give that agreement a place to be tested: the fittings ordered on one bank must reach the builders on the other before the river rises.

name: A Common Civil Service
description: The new offices must be paid for and given authority that a duke cannot revoke whenever a petition displeases him. Local titles and Avian's languages will remain legible in the common register. Rosaline and Montague's private correspondence supplies no mandate for an official marriage: institutions must rest on public articles.

name: Orders in One Chain
description: Iovinus knows how easily a temporary headquarters becomes a permanent government. Vincent's household officers will also have to recognise orders carrying another district's signature. The common staff answers to the constitutional presidency and its published budget. Local service traditions continue within one command.

name: The Final Articles
description: The delegates now have a customs service, public works, common offices and a staff to put under a single constitution. Their final signatures will have a different meaning from the invitation. Each remaining government must explicitly agree to cease being a separate country, transfer its forces and holdings, and accept the initiating House's presidency.

name: One Verenian State
description: The act places the common institutions under one sovereign government, led by the House that called the convention. Provincial customs, courts and languages remain protected by its articles. The dukes' old claims must now be heard within the country they once divided, and the common seal will bind the offices that formerly answered only to their own House.

name: The First Ordinary Budget
description: The ministries must now present the first ordinary budget of the united country. District representatives return with repair estimates and school registers instead of rival declarations of sovereignty. The president's signature will put the new state's promises against its revenues, and every district will want to see where its needs appear in the accounts.

name: The Victory Roll
description: The throne we demanded at Griffenheim was an objective, not an achievement. Before a new imperial title can be proclaimed, the Herzland must be held through settled ownership and effective government, directly or through our dependencies. Let the military and civil offices account for the country behind the victory announcements.

name: The Imperial Coronation
description: Verenia already has its Kaiser. Griffonia has not yet received a Zypressen emperor. Prepare a separate coronation after the Herzland settlement, with a chancery capable of turning the new dignity into government. Neither the ceremony nor the conqueror's surname can supply the consent of every crown beyond the capital.

name: What the Registers Actually Say
description: The imperial archives contain useful knowledge alongside claims of succession. Separate technical records from court rumours, preserve the former household's documented circumstances and improve the means by which offices exchange information. An emperor who wishes to displace a dynasty need not pretend that a missing page proves whatever his courtiers wish to believe.

name: The Crowns Bring Their Own Accounts
description: Our dynasty's dependent governments have treasuries, workshops and obligations of their own. Decide what to offer them: protected local administration with common technical work, or negotiated ministries directing agreed industrial and military business. Family loyalty can begin the conversation. It cannot determine the answer.

name: Freight Before Pageantry
description: Victory has left repair orders competing with the transport of food, machinery and troops. Support engineers and choose where to put the next effort: civilian workshops and better construction, or a permanent board coordinating infrastructure and supplies. An imperial procession cannot carry the freight its timetable displaces.

name: Commissions, Not Family Orders
description: The dynastic rulers have received a proposal for common ministries, and some have returned it with whole paragraphs crossed out. Their treasuries and councils have learned to govern since the conquests that placed them there. Trubach must negotiate with those institutions: a family connection may secure an audience, but it cannot supply the powers his chancery wants.

name: Arsenals and Workshops
description: The war ministry wants weapons that can be repaired with parts made beyond a single arsenal. Expand military production on securely administered land and bring industrial specialists together over common specifications. The dynasty's authority will travel farther if its equipment can survive the journey.

name: An Exchange of Practical Knowledge
description: A common surname does not make every laboratory's instruments interchangeable. The colleges will exchange drawings and teachers with the crowns that signed the technical agreements. Their first task is to make a demonstration repeatable in another country's workshop. Later participants will bring their own apparatus, and their own questions about what the older partners have learned.

name: The Muster and the Harvest
description: The staff's neat mobilisation calendar collides with the work that feeds its soldiers. Dependent rulers are asking what the next campaign will leave available at home. We must choose how to organise our own forces: a stronger permanent cadre with a heavier domestic burden, or limited rotations supported by better training and supply.

name: The Western Approaches
description: Draw up the Aquileian campaign against the governments that now own the intended territories. The old names on a map may no longer name the states we face. Existing allies and dependent realms stand outside the new demands; the general staff must distinguish a frontier from a family possession.

name: Contracts After the Columns
description: The western settlement needs more than the passage of military columns. Give civilian builders dependable contracts and develop construction methods that can turn a damaged district back into a working economy. Our own workshops must support that work without claiming ownership of a neighbour's industry.

name: The Northern Routes
description: Once the western approaches are settled, prepare the routes towards Cloudbury, Vedina, Skyfall and Haukland. Staff work must follow current governments and possession, not the assumption that every old crown still rules. Agreements with allies remain agreements even when their lands appear on an imperial map.

name: The Southern Workshops
description: A settled north permits the staff to turn towards Wingbardy and the southern industrial realms. Their furnaces and workshops matter as much as their palaces. Prepare demands against their actual independent owners without treating the dependent crowns already serving our dynasty as another conquest to repeat.

name: Beyond the Eastern Marches
description: The eastern marches lead towards Hellquill, Longsword, Lushi and the wider eastern principalities. Arrange this campaign only after the earlier theatres are settled. The emperor's ambition reaches across Griffonia; the staff's preparations must still proceed through real territories, maintained routes and governments capable of answering.

name: Seats for the Later Arrivals
description: The campaigns have enlarged the family of dependent crowns. Their new rulers arrive with officials, debts and local promises that the imperial chancery did not write. Trubach will offer them places beside the earlier signatories, with the same need to agree on which powers belong at home and which can be entrusted to common institutions.

name: The Accounts After the Campaigns
description: The regional campaigns have reached a settlement, whether through imperial possession, dependent governments or allied arrangements. Review what our ministries actually control and what remains another government's responsibility. Stable production requires orders that survive the departure of the officer who first demanded them.

name: One Dynasty, Many Countries
description: The imperial crown has acquired a continental task. Its success cannot be measured by calling every dependent government an office or every ally a subject. Consolidate the army's experience and practical support services while preserving an honest account of which powers were negotiated. A Zypressen future must be governed, not merely proclaimed.

name: Reconstruction Office
description: This newly established office coordinates surveys, materials and repair crews. A common schedule helps limited resources reach the work that needs them.

name: Maintained Public Services
description: Regular inspections and dependable repair crews keep wells, dispensaries and public buildings in working order. Local services can now address routine problems before they become emergencies.

name: Common Workshop Standards
description: Shared measurements, inspection routines and apprentice training allow small workshops to fill larger orders with fewer costly mistakes.

name: Veterans in Skilled Work
description: A new placement scheme helps former soldiers find suitable trades. Their practical experience benefits workshop teams, while willing veterans pass useful skills to recruits.

name: Practical Education
description: Teacher courses and accessible lessons give more students the foundations needed for technical study. Researchers can draw on a growing pool of trained assistants.

name: Professional Officer Corps
description: Regular courses and field exercises give officers a common approach to training, administration and command.

name: Permanent Supply Service
description: Reliable inventories and transport schedules reduce waste and make it easier to sustain formations in the field.

name: Integrated Army Staff
description: Commanders and specialist services plan together, test their procedures in joint exercises and pass the lessons on through regular training.

name: District Repair Crews
description: Locally organised crews and a common repair register help damaged buildings return to service sooner.

name: Rural Investment
description: More dependable farm incomes support investment in processing plants and workshops, accelerating civilian factory construction.

name: Practical Education
description: Evening study links basic education to technical work, giving researchers a wider pool of capable assistants.

name: Skilled Reservists
description: Workshop placements and refresher training retain useful skills in civilian production and military service alike.

name: Field Engineer Cadres
description: Experienced engineers teach units to prepare defensive positions more quickly.

name: District Depot Service
description: Better inventories and delivery routines reduce the supplies consumed by our forces.

name: Trained Observer Sections
description: Reliable patrol reporting and local observation improve the army's reconnaissance.

name: Coordinated Field Signals
description: A common reporting network preserves the observers' reconnaissance advantage and improves the rate at which reserves reinforce battles.

name: The Common Translation Office
description: Professional translators maintain consistent versions of common records and technical documents. Their work strengthens confidence in administration and makes research more effective, while the continuing demands of the office consume political effort. Its remit concerns shared business, not the resolution of every linguistic or cultural dispute in Avian.

name: Clerks Appointed by the Towns
description: Common business is explained and recorded through locally appointed clerks familiar to their communities. Their relationships strengthen stability and make it easier to organise political support. They provide a practical means of communication while Avian's broader cultural differences remain matters for further work.

name: The Agreed Budget Protocol
description: Consenting treasuries have accepted a common accounting protocol. Coordinated work accelerates infrastructure construction and the growth of production efficiency, at a political cost to its participants. Avian requires at least one valid partner signature; each other House benefits only through its own assent. The protocol depends on Katrina's preserved three-House charter. Occupation pauses its benefits. War between the Houses, Katrina's replacement, the Second Winterfest Ball or a communist, loyalist or fascist political transition voids its signatures.

name: The Unauthorised Emergency Levy
description: Katrina has allowed the administration to take supplies beyond the agreed obligations. The appropriation increases military output, but undermines stability and increases the burden of civilian goods. All charter benefits, including the common budget, are suspended. Avian must withdraw its exception; any unresolved breaches in Erie or Eyrie must also be settled before shared benefits return.

name: The Common Treasury
description: The common treasury directs funds towards works needed by the whole country, rather than only the former owner of a road.

name: District Credit Associations
description: Local associations finance workshops and suppliers under shared accounting rules.

name: Common Civil Justice
description: The same case is heard under the same law, regardless of the coat of arms above the courthouse.

name: District Self-Government Guarantees
description: Districts retain their institutions, but common civil rights take precedence over local custom.

name: Municipal Housing and Water
description: Towns and rural communities maintain housing, wells and drains under common sanitary rules.

name: Interchangeable Parts
description: Production drawings no longer cease to be useful beyond the workshop that made them.

name: The Verenian Standing Army
description: A common officer corps trains standing formations and maintains unified appointment rolls.

name: District Reserve Service
description: Reservists train near home, while shared depots and instructors connect the districts into a common defence system.

name: The Verenian Audit Office
description: Auditing common expenditure no longer depends on the polite consent of the official who approved it.

name: Emergency Hospital Wards
description: Beds have been found in rooms that were never meant to hold them. Medical supplies and assistance from across the border give Avian's exhausted surgeons time to treat the wounded and return recovering personnel to service. The emergency arrangement lasts 120 days.

name: The House Holds Its Border
description: The answer to Avian's demand has reached the frontier posts. Officers prepare defensive positions and make certain that local orders can still be carried out without permission from Hallhaus. For 180 days, this heightened vigilance strengthens defence and speeds entrenchment.

name: Civilian Border Compact
description: Road crews, workshops and civilian carriers work to schedules recognised on both sides of the border. Each government retains its own authority. Cooperation provides §G+10%§! infrastructure construction speed and §G+5%§! factory output while the signed compact is operational. Capitulation suspends these benefits; war between the signatories, subjugation, disappearance or a change of Avian's political route requires a new agreement.

name: Joint Frontier Inspections
description: Mixed patrols carry officers from both Houses along the same frontier. Neither command can dismiss an incident merely because the other side reported it. Escorts, inquiries and complaints require continuing attention from both courts. The arrangement serves the armistice and ends when a permanent treaty replaces it or the ceasefire itself breaks down. An inspector's presence gives no claim to another House's land.

name: Promises Entered in the Register
description: The duke has heard the petitioners in public. Their expectations steady the country, but answering them requires civilian resources that cannot simply be diverted elsewhere. The register remains open until the promised work is completed or the independent settlement discharges the programme.

name: Roads Worth Repairing
description: The treaty has given engineers and railway planners a reason to invest beyond the next alarm. Infrastructure and railway construction proceed more readily while the two Houses remain independent and their peace holds. These gains belong to the treaty and survive a disagreement over the charter.

name: The Common Courts
description: The charter gives disputes between the Houses an agreed hearing. Enforcing procedure costs the government some freedom of action, but a judgement that binds both courts makes daily life more predictable. These benefits depend on independence, a valid charter and respect for its rulings.

name: The Joint Planning Staff
description: Officers from the participating Houses share supply calculations and operational planning. Compatible procedures improve organisation and reduce supply consumption without dissolving the national armies. The staff's benefits cease when the charter is suspended or its conditions no longer hold.

name: A Presidency Bound by Charter
description: Vincent presides over the council's agreed business within the powers granted by its signatories. The office lends continuity and authority to government, but confers no sovereignty over Eyrie and no hereditary right to command its ruler. This institutional settlement replaces the ordinary common-court arrangement and is suspended if the charter is breached.

name: The Public Council
description: Civic delegates sit within an equal council, making local needs part of the common agenda. Their scrutiny slows the accumulation of political power, while broader confidence and coordinated civilian works strengthen stability and construction. The council replaces the ordinary common-court arrangement; its benefits require a charter respected by the rulers themselves.

name: Shared Technical Services
description: Common specifications, accessible technical records and regular exchanges between workshops improve factory output and the growth of production efficiency. The offices serve the independent signatories together. Their benefits depend on the continued operation of the charter.

name: The Duke's Exception
description: Vincent has placed a personal undertaking above the common court's judgement. His immediate freedom to act has grown, but confidence in his promises has suffered. All charter benefits are suspended until he withdraws the exception and accepts the ruling. The friendship treaty itself remains in force while its conditions hold.

name: Avian Provisional Administration
description: Appeals, public accounts and requisitions must be reconciled before the provisional frontier can disappear. The work consumes officials and construction capacity until incorporation is completed.

name: The Avian District Charter
description: Local courts and workshop contracts survive incorporation. They make rebuilding dependable, but petitions and appeals remain obligations the central government cannot simply dismiss.

name: The Avian Ducal Commission
description: A single commission coordinates workshops and military supply. Its orders are effective; its distance from the inhabitants remains a source of resentment.

name: The Obligations of the Campaign
description: Clear commitments to suppliers and supporters make mobilisation and planning faster. Maintaining them limits Vincent's political freedom: the campaign consumes promises as surely as provisions, and those who provide either expect to be remembered.

name: Rights in Defeat
description: Local guarantees give the defeated districts grounds to trust reconstruction and resume building. Respecting their rights strengthens stability at the cost of some ducal freedom of action. These protections must withstand demands from the winners as well as complaints from the losers.

name: The Ducal Commissioners
description: Vincent's commissioners coordinate military organisation and industrial output through direct authority. Their capacity to get work done comes with unrest among those expected to accept instructions without a comparable voice in making them.

name: The Chartered Ducal Settlement
description: Vincent's rule over the settled districts is bound by their charters. Predictable obligations strengthen stability, construction and the economy of army supply while limiting his political discretion. This settlement concerns Erie and its defeated rival; it grants no authority over Avian.

name: The Consolidated Ducal Administration
description: A permanent central administration channels industrial work, military organisation and political authority through the duke. Vincent can make his decisions felt more strongly, but the governed districts remain uneasy about how little stands between his favour and their fortunes.

name: The Patron's Reward
description: Vincent has rewarded wartime service with the contested estate. His fighting supporters draw confidence from that loyalty. Others see a government whose undertakings depend on which side of the audience chamber they can enter, weakening stability and consuming political authority.

name: A Hearing Even Against the Victor
description: The estate claim must stand on evidence, including where it challenges the duke's patron. Greater confidence in property and government strengthens stability and the growth of production efficiency. Service to Erie remains an obligation for Erie to honour, without making another household its payment.

name: An Accountable Muster
description: The rolls are open to scrutiny beyond the barracks. Local records and service returns must agree, and missing entries require an answer. Reliable figures accelerate mobilisation and strengthen stability, while maintaining that accountability consumes a continuing share of the government's political effort.

name: The Officers' Confidence
description: An army commission has taken responsibility for correcting the muster. Professional review improves training and organisation, strengthening the officers' confidence in their service. Keeping the inquiry within the army unsettles those whose objections remain outside the barracks gates, weakening public stability.

name: Civilian Scrutiny of Defence
description: Local representatives have a recognised place in reviewing the demands of defence. Better justified deliveries reduce supply consumption, while confidence in the procedure strengthens stability. Regular scrutiny requires political effort every day, including those when the frontier gives no immediate cause for alarm.

name: A Command with Defined Responsibilities
description: The professional command is responsible for maintaining readiness within acknowledged limits. Clear responsibilities accelerate planning and improve army organisation. Officers must arrange their procedures accordingly, accepting that military competence includes knowing when an emergency power has expired.

name: Requisitions Without Release
description: The duke has protected the command's refusal to return civilian workshops. Retaining their capacity increases military factory output, but undermines stability and increases the burden of civilian goods. All shared charter benefits are suspended. Withdrawing this order resolves Eyrie's breach; any separate Erie exception must also be settled before common benefits can return.

name: The Civilian Release Schedule
description: Ordinary administration and economic responsibilities are returning to civilian hands. Greater confidence supports stability and civilian factory construction, while the army loses some of the organisational advantages of keeping the country on an emergency footing.

name: Military Tutelage of the Districts
description: Standing commands govern the settled districts. They strengthen army organisation and planning, but civilian life must support a costly military apparatus. The burden on consumer goods and the loss of public stability accompany the order Iovinus has chosen to retain.

name: Post Beyond the Headquarters
description: Private civilian correspondence can circulate without a commander's countersignature. Knowledge travels more freely, improving research. Maintaining a reliable service outside military control requires continuing political attention.

name: The Commander's Countersignature
description: The command continues to supervise correspondence. Its familiarity with the movement of information helps planning, while the knowledge that private words may be examined deepens public distrust and weakens stability.

name: Reservists Without a Trade
description: Civilian boards must absorb returning reservists without the promised central investment in training and capacity. Uncertain livelihoods weaken stability and slow civilian factory construction. A release order has provided freedom from one obligation without the means to begin another life.

name: The Army's First Claim on Production
description: Command reserves workshop time for military orders. Arms production benefits, while civilian factory construction falls behind. The government has chosen to satisfy readiness first and leave ordinary repairs and investment to compete for the hours that remain.

name: Civilian Contracts Under Military Rule
description: Negotiated contracts give civilian workshops a defined place within the military settlement. More dependable supply reduces waste and improves the growth of production efficiency. Maintaining the bargain costs continuing political effort and does not abolish the district commands.

name: A Limited Guardianship
description: The regency cares for Grover while administering Herzland in trust. Its authority carries an obligation to prepare a government that can stand without its guardians.

name: The Adult Sovereign's Transition
description: Grover has reached adulthood. The remaining work belongs to ministries, treaties and the restoration of peace; it confers no further right to direct his upbringing.

name: The Verenian-Imperial Market
description: Verenian workshops and Herzland buyers continue to trade under an agreement between independent governments. The old regency's accounts have become the records of a shared commercial undertaking.

name: The Defence Compact
description: Verenia and the restored Empire prepare their defence as allies. Their staffs share responsibilities without making either government the other's guardian.

name: The Open Court's Legacy
description: Grover remembers witnesses who were permitted to disagree with the court. The habit of hearing them has followed him into his own government.

name: The Managed Court's Legacy
description: Grover learned to work through an orderly circle of advisers. Their discipline remains useful, and the voices outside that circle remain a question his own reign must answer.

name: A Law Above Favour
description: An inconvenient judgement once bound the regent's own supporter. Grover carries that precedent into an imperial court whose friends must now discover that it binds them too.

name: The Patrons' Precedent
description: The regency protected a useful supporter when the law became inconvenient. Grover remembers both the loyalty that protection secured and the petitioner who left without an ordinary hearing.

name: Provincial Public Service
description: Local courts and reconstruction offices share a public record of contracts, claims and completed work. A stalled project has an office answerable for it, and a petitioner can follow its progress beyond the palace gates.

name: Institutions of the Settlement
description: The restored state rests on working institutions: workshops that train apprentices, laboratories that exchange their findings and ministries that can carry out a decision without waiting for another ceremony.

name: Aquileian Scholarly Tradition
description: Erie's schools use an Aquileian written standard to connect elementary teaching with scientific literature. Teacher training and accessible books give local students a firmer foundation for advanced study.

name: Herzland Scholarly Tradition
description: Eyrie's Griffish curriculum draws on the Herzland's scholarly inheritance. Clear textbooks and trained instructors connect parish classrooms with technical and scientific study.

name: A Bilingual Public Education
description: Aquileian and Griffish share a place in public education. Training teachers in both languages takes resources, but gives more families confidence in the schools and more pupils access to further study.

name: Public Scholarship Endowment
description: Scholarships awarded through open examinations support a continuing supply of teachers, researchers, and civil servants. Their obligation to serve public institutions turns educational opportunity into lasting civic capacity.

name: Griffenheim Reconstruction Commission
description: A temporary civilian commission coordinates repairs after the defensive war. Its staff consume political resources; its authority has a fixed expiry and rests on peace and Erie's actual control of Griffenheim.

name: The Commission's Final Year
description: A final funded year brings stronger repair teams and a small technical research office. Its political expense cannot be renewed indefinitely. At the deadline, peaceful reconstruction passes automatically to ordinary civilian services.

name: Civilian Reconstruction Services
description: Published technical records and trained workshop crews continue serving the public after the temporary commission has closed. Their benefit lasts two years and carries no special political authority.

name: Verenia Technical Protocol
description: Consenting charter governments, or the authorized research offices of their legitimate unified successor, exchange engineering papers and production standards. The finite programme grants no territory or dynastic authority. Unified participation ends if the founding, charter or homeland conditions fail.

name: The Limited Regency
description: Erie and Eyrie have separately accepted guardianship of the living minor Grover VI in Avian. An independent House signs through its government; a lawfully absorbed House votes through its estates. Katrina governs within those limits. Majority, death or loss of the required conditions ends the authority to act; old signatures alone cannot sustain its benefits.

name: The Civil Herzland Compact
description: Erie and Eyrie have separately consented to a civilian settlement. Independent governments and the estates of lawfully absorbed Houses answer for their own undertakings. Repairs and infrastructure receive support while the charter, sovereign homeland and current consent remain valid.

name: Verenia's Constitutional Guarantees
description: The Houses' reserved institutions bind the settlement, including an adult constitutional monarch. Independent partners keep their governments; constituent estates retain their agreed voice within the unified country. Reliable obligations strengthen stability and production, while respecting them consumes political influence.

name: The Joint Supply Offices
description: Agreed schedules and supply arrangements let Avian prepare plans faster and consume fewer supplies. Keeping the offices accountable to the settlement requires continuing political work. Their remit grants no command over an independent House's army.

name: The Territorial Reserve Articles
description: Reserves organised around familiar ground strengthen defence on our core territory and help formations recover. Planning proceeds more slowly as local readiness takes precedence over the convenience of a single timetable. The arrangement develops Katrina's reservist tradition within the agreed limits.

name: Common Customs
description: One schedule and compatible industrial standards reduce duplicated work.

name: Interprovincial Works
description: Shared contracts keep workshops and roads useful across the former boundaries.

name: Building the Common Service
description: The new offices require political attention while they establish reliable common records.

name: Constitutional Joint Command
description: The shared staff serves the presidency while respecting local service traditions.

name: The Founded Verenian State
description: The founding administration joins industry and defence under one government. Its first ordinary budget is still being prepared.

name: Verenian Common Institutions
description: Local customs and languages endure within one constitutional state. Working schools, offices, workshops and a unified staff give its presidency lasting substance.

name: The Imperial Chancery
description: A new imperial office lends stability and political authority to Trubach's coronation. It operates while his independent government and effective control of Griffenheim through Verenia or its subjects endure.

name: An Autonomous Dynastic Compact
description: This dependent government has accepted common technical work while retaining its own administration. Stable local orders favour civilian construction, at an ongoing political cost. No territory or sovereignty is transferred by the compact.

name: Negotiated Common Ministries
description: This government has expressly delegated agreed industrial and technical responsibilities to common ministries. Military production and research benefit, while the administration consumes political effort. Its crown, territory and existing subject relationship remain intact.

name: The Working Dynastic Network
description: At least one eligible crown has accepted an institutional agreement. Exchange accelerates research and production efficiency growth, with a political cost to the imperial government. Refusal by every partner leaves no network to administer.

name: The Freight Coordination Board
description: Permanent dispatchers coordinate infrastructure work and reduce the waste of military supplies. Their authority concerns our transport administration; they have not been given another crown's railways.

name: A Permanent Campaign Cadre
description: Standing officers and specialists improve organisation and planning. Maintaining this cadre strains domestic stability. The measure reorganises our own army and does not conscript a dependent country's forces by decree.

name: Rotations the Districts Can Sustain
description: Limited rotations and practical training reduce the time needed to prepare our soldiers and the supplies they consume. The staff accepts a less ambitious standing commitment in exchange for dependable provision.

name: Orders That Outlast the Campaign
description: Predictable industrial orders support civilian construction and a higher production efficiency ceiling. The imperial administration is learning to purchase sustained output instead of treating every workshop as a temporary military store.
